headline: Approved $2,979,000 for McTaggart Pond Dam removal, $260,000 for Riverfront Park stage, and $140,000 for a police mental health program.
summary: Council also approved a $66,007.45 transfer for Fiscal Year 2026 budget deficits and $20,134 for ballistic shields. It sent an $11,400,000 water loan order to a first and second reading and referred five mayoral appointments to committee.
decisions: Approved minutes of the October 20, 2026 meeting, 10-0.
Referred five mayoral appointments and reappointments to the Appointments Committee.
Approved $2,979,000 in grant funds to complete construction of the McTaggart Pond Dam removal and Phillips Brook restoration, by unanimous consent 9-0.
Approved $133,700 in grant funds for a feasibility study on removing the Overlook Reservoir Dam and Dike, by unanimous consent 9-0.
Approved $150,000 in grant funds to advance design and permitting for two replacement culverts along Ashby West Road, by unanimous consent 9-0.
Approved $22,658.40 from TNC per ride assessment funds for road repaving, by unanimous consent 9-0.
Approved $260,000 in grant funds toward construction of the Riverfront Park Stage, by unanimous consent 9-0.
Approved $40,000 from reserve funds for title searches, appraisals, and easements for new sidewalks to Memorial Middle School, by unanimous consent 9-0.
Approved $64,575 from reserve funds for DEP clean-up costs at several city-owned sites, by unanimous consent 9-0.
Approved $66,007.45 from reserve funds to cover Fiscal Year 2026 budget deficits, as amended, by unanimous consent 9-0.
Sent an $11,400,000 water projects loan order to a first and second reading and ordered it advertised, 9-0.
Adopted a resolution thanking and honoring Ronald B. Ingemie, 9-0.
Approved $20,134 in Byrne grant funds to buy ballistic shields and shield lights, 9-0.
Approved $140,000 in Jail Diversion Program funds for a mental health professional with the Police Department and crisis training, 9-0.
Referred order to authorize acquiring 98 Maverick Street for One Dollar to City Property.
Adopted a resolution requesting the Council fulfill requirements of the Riverfront Park stage grant, 9-0.
Referred ordinance amending chapters 3 and 169 of the City Code, the parking ordinance, to Legislative Affairs.
Referred Unitil petition for new utility pole #19A on Crawford St. to a public hearing on November 17, 2026.
Referred Unitil petition for new utility pole #2A on Wilmot St. to a public hearing on November 17, 2026.
Referred request for No Parking signs on both sides of Boutelle St. to Public Safety.
Referred request for a state special legislation petition allowing digital posting of City legal notices to Legislative Affairs.
Scheduled an executive session with the Mayor on pending litigation in Suarez v. City of Fitchburg for November 17, 2026.

City of Fitchburg  
                             Massachusetts 01420  
 
                     CITY COUNCIL  
            
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Fitchburg was held at the Legislative Building 
at 700 Main Street and over the Zoom meeting platform and live streamed at FATV Studios, 
Fitchburg, on November 4, 2026.   
 
The meeting was called to orde r by President Zarrella at 7:01 P.M.  The meeting opened with a 
salute to the Flag led by Councilor Green. The City Clerk called the roll 10 Councilors were present, 
(Councilor Cragin absent). Board consists of 11 members.  
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
I. PUBLIC FORUM 
  
No one spoke during Public Forum. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
II. ANNOUNCEMENTS 
 
The next meeting of the Widowed Helping Widowed Support Group will take place on Thursday, 
November 12 from 4 until 5:30 p.m. in Room 205 at the Fitchburg State University Recreation 
Center, 130 North Street. Kelley Lynn, Kathy Boisvert, and Bernie Schultz will co-facilitate the 
meeting. 
---- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------  
Fitchburg City Councilor Bernie Schultz is hosting a City Council Community Meeting on 
Monday, November 9, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. right here in the Legislative Building, 700 Main Street.  
Sizer School Executive Director Michelle Paranto and Ashby Evergreen Charter School 
Representative Heather Perry will make presentations and then answer questions following their 
presentations. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
 
 
 
Councilors at Large 
    Sally H. Cragin 
Amy L. Green 
Kevin T. Starr  
Elizabeth R. Walsh 
Anthony M. Zarrella 
 
President 
Anthony M. Zarrella 
 
Vice President 
Derrick J. Cruz 
         Ward Councilors 
   Ward 1 – Bernard J. Schultz III 
   Ward 2 – Paul R. Beauchemin 
   Ward 3 – Joseph S. Bowen, Jr. 
   Ward 4 – Andrew J. Van Hazinga 
   Ward 5 – Marisa R. Fleming 
   Ward 6 – Derrick J. Cruz
Good evening, President Zarrella, members of the City Council, and members of the public. 
I would like to take a few moments this evening to recognize the tremendous effort that went into 
administering yesterday's November 3, 2026 State Election here in the City of Fitchburg. 
We experienced an exceptionally busy Election Day, with tremendous voter participation 
throughout our City. Conducting an election of this magnitude requires months of preparation, 
coordination, training, and the dedication of so many individuals. 
First and foremost, I want to extend my heartfelt appreciation to our election workers. 
Our election workers dedicated 17½ hours on Election Day, beginning at 6:00 AM and continuing 
until approximately 11:30 PM. Their commitment goes well beyond Election Day itself. They 
attend training sessions, prepare for changes in election procedures, and work tirelessly to ensure 
that every voter has the opportunity to cast their ballot. 
This election presented additional challenges, including a three-card ballot and nine statewide 
ballot questions. Our election workers handled these responsibilities with professionalism, 
patience, and dedication. I cannot thank them enough. 
I would also like to clarify something for the public regarding the ballot tabulators. Because each 
voter received three ballot cards, the number displayed on the tabulator represents the total number 
of ballot cards processed, not the number of individual voters. I want to make sure residents 
understand that distinction when looking at the numbers displayed on the machines. 
I would also like to recognize the many City departments whose cooperation is essential to the 
success of our elections. 
To the Fitchburg Public Schools, Superintendent Thompson, Facilities Director Daniel Outerson, 
and the entire custodial team, thank you for making our school buildings available as polling 
locations and ensuring that they were prepared, accessible, and ready to welcome voters. Your 
coordination, attention to detail, and willingness to assist are greatly appreciated. 
To DPW Commissioner Nick Erickson and the entire Department of Public Works, thank you for 
the tremendous logistical support involved in preparing our polling locations, transporting 
equipment, setting up voting areas, and assisting with the many operational needs of Election Day. 
To our Parks and Recreation Department, thank you for your cooperation and assistance in 
providing and preparing facilities used for voting. 
To the Fitchburg Police Department, thank you for your presence and assistance in maintaining 
safe and accessible polling locations throughout the City. 
To the Fitchburg Fire Department, thank you for your continued cooperation and assistance, 
particularly in providing nighttime lighting and ensuring that generators were fueled, maintained, 
and ready to operate throughout the election. 
I also want to recognize the dedicated staff of the City Clerk's Office. The weeks leading up to an 
election are extraordinarily demanding, and this election was certainly no exception.
From early voting and vote-by-mail processing to equipment preparation, election worker 
coordination, advance deposit procedures, and Election Day operations, our staff worked tirelessly 
to ensure that everything was ready. 
Betsy, Lily, Rachelle, and Maribel, I am extremely proud of each of you. Your dedication, 
teamwork, professionalism, and willingness to go above and beyond are what make our office 
successful. I truly could not do this without you. 
Finally, I want to thank the voters of Fitchburg. 
Your participation in the democratic process is what makes all of this work meaningful. Whether 
you voted early, by mail, or at the polls yesterday, thank you for taking the time to exercise your 
right to vote. 
While Election Day has concluded, our work continues. Our office is now reviewing the election-
night hand-count tally sheets, write-in tally sheets, and required election paperwork to reconcile 
and finalize the election results. This process must be completed so that the official results can be 
certified and submitted to the Commonwealth no later than November 18, 2026. 
Administering a successful election is truly a Citywide effort, and I am grateful to everyone who 
contributed. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
III. REPORT OF THE APPOINTMENTS COMMITTEE 
 
Appointments Committee did not convene because the meeting agenda had not been officially 
posted. Appointment will be taken up at the next meeting.

Affairs Eco One Stop Grant to complete the construction phase of the McTaggart 
Pond Dam Removal and Phillips Brook Restoration Project. 
 (Be Adopted)
173-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg appropriate grant funds in the approximate 
amount of ONE HUNDRED THIRTY-THREE THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED 
DOLLARS ($133,700) from the Executive Office of Energy and Environmental 
Affairs Eco One Stop Grant to conduct a feasibility study to assess removal of the 
Overlook Reservoir Dam and Dike, or lowering the normal pool elevations. 
 (Be Adopted) 
 
174-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg appropriate grant funds in the approximate 
amount of ONE HUNDRED FIFTY THOUSAND DOLLARS ($150,000) to

EMPLOYEE BENEFITS – Workers Compensation  $139,810.35

Report read and accepted. Orders 172-26 through 178-26 adopted and 179-26 adopted as amended

Orders signed by the Mayor November 12, 2026 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
 
180-26. LOAN ORDER: that Loan Order #019-25, which was ordered by this Council on 
March 18, 2025 and authorized a borrowing of $11,400,000 for various water 
projects, is hereby amended by replacing it in its entirety to read as follows:  
 
  ORDERED:  That $11,400,000 aggregate amount is appropriated for the following 
  projects, including all costs incidental and related thereto, which amount may be  
  apportioned to such projects as needed to accomplish the projects: (i) rehabilitation 
  and/or upgrade of the Meetinghouse Gatehouse and Mare Meadow/Bickford Pump                
                        Station, at an estimated cost of $4,220,000; (ii) Main Street water main replacement  
   project, at an estimated cost of $3,290,000, which amount is expected to be used in  
addition to certain American Rescue Plan Act funds available for the project; (iii)  
Regional Water Treatment Plant roof replacement and/or weatherproofing project, 
at an estimated cost of $740,000; (iv) Water Street water main replacement project, 
at an estimated cost of $1,750,000; and (v) Exeter Street and Rodimon Avenue 
water main replacement projects, including fire hydrants and domestic/fire service 
lines, at an estimated cost of $1,400,000, which amount is expected to be used in 
addition certain other funds available through the City’s annual operating budget; 
and that to meet this appropriation the Treasurer with the approval of the Mayor is 
authorized to borrow $11,400,000 under G.L. c.44, §8 or any other enabling 
authority; that the Mayor is authorized to contract for and expend any federal or 
state aid available for the projects; that the Mayor is authorized to take any other 
action necessary to carry out the projects; and that the Treasurer is authorized to file 
an application with the Municipal Finance Oversight Board to qualify under 
Chapter 44A of the General Laws any or all of the bonds authorized by this order 
and to provide such information  
and execute such documents as the Municipal Finance Oversight Board may require  
for these purposes. 
(Be Adopted – First Reading to be advertised) 
 
Report read and accepted. Loan Order was sent to a first and second reading and ordered 
advertised by unanimous consent 9/0. 9 members present. Board consists of 11 members.

Legislative Affairs Committee   
Meeting of November 4, 2026 
Oral Report 
 
181-26. RESOLUTION: NOW BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED that the City Council of 
Fitchburg thanks and honors Ronald B. Ingemie for his distinguished service and 
lasting contributions to the City and its residents; and 
 
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that a portrait of Ron Ingemie and a plaque 
memorializing his service, the same to be donated by private parties, be displayed in 
the Legislative Building. 
 
Report read and accepted. Resolution adopted by unanimous consent 9/0. 9 members present. 
Board consists of 11 members. 
 
Resolution signed by the Mayor November 12, 2026. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
VII. ORDERS – FINANCE 
 
Motion and second for suspension of rules for Orders 184 – 26, 185-26 and Resolution 187-26 by  
Unanimous consent 9/0. 9 members present. Board consists of 11 members. 
 
184-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg hereby approves the expenditure of funds 
from the Department of Justice Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant 
(JAG) in the approximate amount of TWENTY THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED 
THIRTY-FOUR DOLLARS ($20,134) for the purchase of ballistic shields and 
shield lights. 
 (Suspension of Rules) 
 
Motion and second to adopt order by unanimous consent 9/0. 9 members present. Board consists of

185-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg hereby approves the expenditure of funds 
from the Department of Mental Health Jail Diversion Program (JDP) in the 
approximate amount of ONE HUNDRED FORTY THOUSAND DOLLARS 
($140,000) to fund the placement of a mental health professional embedded with 
the Police Department, as well as training for the purpose of maintaining the Police 
Department Crisis Intervention Team (CIT), supporting individuals in mental health 
crises other disturbances. 
 (Suspension of Rules) 
 
Motion and second to adopt order by unanimous consent 9/0. 9 members present. Board consists of

Order stands referred to City Property:

North Registry of Deeds in Book 1309, Page 167, appended hereto, and to authorize

and

out this order.

Resolution

(Finance)  
 
Motion and second to adopt resolution by unanimous consent 9/0. 9 members present. Board  
consists of 11 members. 
 
Resolution signed by the Mayor November 12, 2026. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
X. ORDINANCE 
 
188-26. AN ORDINANCE: President Zarrella on behalf of Michaela Horn, Treasurer, to 
amend chapters 3 and 169 of the City Code as outlined in the enclosed ordinance. 
 Parking Ordinance 
 (Legislative Affairs) 
 
 
XI. PETITIONS 
 
189-26.  CRAWFORD ST – Unitil petition for a new proposed pole #19A on Crawford St., 
approximately 380’ from Blueberry Lane and approximately 2885’ from Airport 
Blvd. 
 Crawford St. 
 (Refer to Public Hearing November 17, 2026)
190-26. WILMOT ST – Unitil petition for a new proposed pole #2A on Wilmot St.,

Discussion to determine a date for an Executive Session with the Mayor pursuant to M.G.L. c.

Executive session scheduled for November 17, 2026 following the Regular meeting of City

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
Next Regular City Council Meeting 
Tuesday, November 17, 2026 7:00 PM
